neighbours.label: nouns and verbs describing a measurable physical quantity or condition of a body or substance (the amount of mucus increases, soil moisture, muscles tightened); everyday actions and non-physical nouns stay low
fire: During exercise, the volume of sweat increases and the skin becomes damp.
Water the seedlings when the soil humidity drops below a safe level.
Squeeze your thigh muscles and hold the position for a slow count of five.
After a meal, the amount of saliva rises and swallowing becomes easier.
The doctor checked whether the swelling in his ankle had become larger.
运动时汗液量明显增加，皮肤变得潮湿。
Plant care: light: full sun. Soil moisture: dry to medium.
As the solution cools, its viscosity increases and it pours more slowly.
quiet: During the holidays, the number of visitors increases and the shops stay open late.
Call the plumber when the landlord says the repair can wait no longer.
Read the instructions and hold the box steady while you open it.
After a meal, the family usually goes for a walk around the block.
The doctor checked whether the clinic had received the new forms.
周末时游客数量明显增加，商店营业到很晚。
Plant care: price: five dollars. Pot: plastic, green.
As the meeting continues, the agenda grows longer and people leave early.

short: physical quantity/condition of body or substance
